title: NEB Class 12 Chemistry — Chemical Thermodynamics — 2023
origin: curated NEB-pattern set for class-12 chemistry thermodynamics

questions.solution:
First law: energy is conserved — $\Delta U = q + w$ (heat added to the system plus work done on it equals the change in internal energy).
For a reversible change $w = -\int_{V_1}^{V_2} P_{\text{ext}}\,dV = -\int P\,dV$. For an ideal gas $P = nRT/V$, so $w_{\text{rev}} = -nRT\int_{V_1}^{V_2} dV/V = -nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$.
Isothermal means $T$ constant, and for an ideal gas $U$ depends only on $T$, so $\Delta U = 0$. Then $q = -w = nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$ — all the heat absorbed is converted into expansion work.
questions.question: State the first law of thermodynamics. Derive the expression for pressure–volume work in a reversible isothermal expansion of $n$ moles of an ideal gas from $V_1$ to $V_2$, and give the heat absorbed.

questions.solution: Moles of gas fall from 4 to 2, so disorder decreases: $\Delta S < 0$. $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$; at low $T$ the negative $\Delta H$ dominates, so $\Delta G < 0$ and the reaction is spontaneous. (At high temperature the $-T\Delta S > 0$ term wins and it becomes non-spontaneous — why ammonia is made at moderate temperatures.)
questions.question: For the reaction $\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}$, with $\Delta H = -92.4\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$, what are the signs of $\Delta S$ and $\Delta G$ at low temperature, and is the reaction spontaneous?

questions.solution:
Entropy $S$ measures the number of microscopic arrangements of a system — the degree of disorder; $\Delta S = q_{\text{rev}}/T$.
Second law: the entropy of an isolated system (the universe) never decreases; every spontaneous process increases total entropy.
If heat $q$ flows from hot ($T_h$) to cold ($T_c$), $\Delta S = -q/T_h + q/T_c = q(1/T_c - 1/T_h) > 0$ since $T_c < T_h$ — allowed. Reverse flow would give $\Delta S < 0$, forbidden in an isolated system. Refrigerators achieve it only by doing external work, increasing entropy elsewhere.
questions.question: Define entropy. State the second law of thermodynamics and use it to explain why heat flows spontaneously from a hot body to a cold body but never the reverse.

questions.solution:
Combustion: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH(l) + 3O_2(g) \rightarrow 2CO_2(g) + 3H_2O(l)}$.
$\Delta H_c^\circ = \sum \Delta H_f^\circ(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta H_f^\circ(\text{reactants}) = [2(-393.5) + 3(-285.8)] - [(-277.7) + 0]$.
$= (-787.0 - 857.4) + 277.7 = -1644.4 + 277.7 = -1366.7\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$.
Molar mass of ethanol $= 46\,\mathrm{g/mol}$, so $9.2\,\mathrm{g} = 0.2\,\mathrm{mol}$. Heat released $= 0.2 \times 1366.7 = 273.3\,\mathrm{kJ}$.
questions.question: Standard enthalpies of formation: $\Delta H_f^\circ[\mathrm{CO_2(g)}] = -393.5$, $\Delta H_f^\circ[\mathrm{H_2O(l)}] = -285.8$, $\Delta H_f^\circ[\mathrm{C_2H_5OH(l)}] = -277.7\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$ (all in kJ/mol). Calculate the standard enthalpy of combustion of ethanol, and the heat released by burning $9.2\,\mathrm{g}$ of ethanol.
